comparison.objective: Connects an M12 sensor cable while preventing a loose sensor barrel from rotating; the candidate adjusts a stop screw and locks it with its jam nut.
comparison.physical_skill: PR-1540 directly holds a large sensor body while turning a coupling ring; the candidate must keep a driver seated in the screw while a second tool turns a concentric thin nut against it.
comparison.success_condition: PR-1540 succeeds when the connector is threaded tight, the cap is stored, and hands withdraw; the candidate additionally requires a retained angular setpoint and three released functional cycles.
comparison.reason: The close shared feature is bimanual reaction-torque control, but connector assembly against a stabilized body does not test coupled screw–nut setpoint preservation.

review_notes: Very close skill neighbor: hold loose proximity sensor while turning threaded cable coupling ring; actual original says ring drags sensor unless restrained. Compare two-tool coupled setpoint preservation versus body stabilization for assembly; do NOT assume industry, gripper geometry, angle target or cycles alone are sufficient novelty.
